mainTopic: How far suspicion reaches: רבא's penalty on a cheating seller, and the משנה about שביעית, מעשרות and טהרות with its explanations and authorship
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a man who sold forbidden fat as permitted fat. רבא banned him from selling even nuts. רב פפא asks whether that follows רבי יהודה, and רבא answers that it follows רבי שמעון, because the man used nuts to bribe butchers' children into bringing him the forbidden fat. Next comes a new משנה. Suspicion about שביעית and suspicion about מעשרות do not carry over to each other. Suspicion about either carries over to טהרות, but suspicion about טהרות does not carry back. A suspected person may not judge or testify about the matter he is suspected of. The גמרא explains each part: מעשר feels serious because it must be eaten in ירושלים, and שביעית feels serious because it cannot be redeemed. Torah law outweighs rabbinic law. A contradiction from a ברייתא is answered in two ways. Finally, רבי יוחנן says the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and two versions identify the disagreeing חכמים as רבי יהודה or רבי מאיר. Students then begin to argue over which version is right, and that argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא bans a cheating seller from selling even nuts
steps.stepSummary: A man sold forbidden thigh-area fat as permitted intestinal fat, and רבא penalized him by forbidding him to sell even nuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone sold the forbidden fat of the thigh area as if it were the permitted fat of the intestines. רבא penalized him and did not let him sell even nuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story and reports רבא's ruling: a man caught selling forbidden fat as permitted fat may not sell even nuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nuts have no connection to forbidden fat, so this penalty looks unusually broad. That puzzle sets up רב פפא's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat of the thigh area (kidney fat), which is forbidden חֵלֶב
Fat of the intestines, which is permitted

phrases.english: fat of the thigh in place of fat of the intestines,
phrases.notes: This continues a story that started just before: a man was selling this forbidden fat and calling it the permitted kind.

phrases.english: Rava penalized him, so that he could not sell
even nuts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by finishing a story about a cheating seller that began just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller caught passing off forbidden fat as permitted fat is penalized and may not sell even nuts.

steps.title: רב פפא asks which opinion רבא followed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests רבא's broad ban must follow רבי יהודה. But if so, the man should be banned from selling even water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Whose opinion are you following? רבי יהודה's? If you follow רבי יהודה, you should ban even water and salt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's ruling. It seems to follow רבי יהודה's strict view, but it does not go as far as רבי יהודה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a suspected seller may not sell anything at all, not even water and salt. רבי שמעון limits the ban to items connected to the suspicion. Banning nuts looks too broad for רבי שמעון and too narrow for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
Water and salt, the simplest items, which רבי יהודה also bans

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying רבא was too strict. He is saying the ruling fits neither opinion: it is too strict for רבי שמעון and not strict enough for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
According to whom? According to Rabbi Yehuda?
If according to Rabbi Yehuda,
then even water and salt too!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה, that such a seller can't sell even water and salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֲפִילּוּ מַיִם וָמֶלַח נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Banning unrelated items fits only רבי יהודה. But רבי יהודה would ban everything, even water and salt, so the ruling fits neither opinion.

steps.title: רבא explains: the nuts were the tool he used to cheat
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he follows רבי שמעון. The nuts are connected to the sin, because the man used them to bribe butchers' children into bringing him forbidden fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I follow רבי שמעון, and I penalized him only in connection with the sin itself. Children love nuts. This man went and tricked the butchers' children by tempting them with nuts. They brought him the forbidden thigh fat, and he sold it as permitted intestinal fat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. He follows רבי שמעון, and the nuts really are tied to the sin, because the man used them to get the forbidden fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון bans only items connected to the suspicion. רבא shows that the nuts fit this test: they were how the man got the forbidden fat in the first place. So the ban is not an extra-broad penalty. It cuts off his method of cheating.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי שמעון, a suspected person is banned only from items tied to his sin. An item that seems unrelated can still count if it was the tool he used to commit the sin.

phrases.english: Really, it is according to Rabbi Shimon,
and we penalize him in connection with the prohibition itself.
Ordinary children are enticed by nuts,
and he goes and misleads the butchers' children,
and entices them with nuts,
and they bring him fat of the thigh,
and he sells it as fat of the intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וּבְאִיסּוּרָא דְּגוּפֵיהּ קָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the banned item is really connected to the sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nuts have nothing to do with forbidden fat, so banning them must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nuts were the bribe he used to get the forbidden fat, so banning them fits רבי שמעון's rule of banning only related items.

steps.title: משנה: suspicion in one area does not spread to another
steps.stepSummary: Suspicion about שביעית does not make a person suspected about מעשרות, and suspicion about מעשרות does not make him suspected about שביעית. Someone suspected about either is suspected about טהרות, but not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone suspected of not keeping the laws of שביעית is not suspected about מעשרות, and someone suspected about מעשרות is not suspected about שביעית. Someone suspected about either one is suspected about טהרות. But some people are suspected about טהרות and are not suspected about either of the others.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how far suspicion reaches between three areas of halacha: שביעית, מעשרות and טהרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביעית and מעשרות are kept separate, so suspicion in one does not carry over to the other. טהרות is treated as the lighter area in people's eyes: anyone lax about the first two is surely lax about טהרות. Being lax about טהרות, however, does not prove a person is lax about the others.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspected, not trusted to keep a certain halacha
The seventh year, whose produce has special laws
Laws of ritual purity, such as selling impure food as pure

steps.confusionAlert: The suspicion about טהרות goes in one direction only. Being suspected about שביעית or מעשרות makes a person suspected about טהרות, but being suspected about טהרות does not make him suspected about the other two.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who is suspect regarding the Sabbatical Year
is not suspect regarding tithes;
one who is suspect regarding tithes
is not suspect regarding the Sabbatical Year.
One who is suspect regarding this or that
phrases.notes: Literally 'this and that'. It means someone suspected about either שביעית or מעשרות.

phrases.english: is suspect regarding ritual purity;
but there is one who is suspect regarding ritual purity

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ חָשׁוּד לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: and is suspect neither regarding this nor regarding that.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית אֵינוֹ חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It stays with the theme of suspicion but moves to a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspicion about שביעית and suspicion about מעשרות do not carry over to each other. Either one carries over to טהרות, but suspicion about טהרות does not carry back to them.

steps.title: משנה's general rule: a suspected person may not judge or testify
steps.stepSummary: Anyone suspected about a certain matter may not judge cases or testify about that matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule: someone suspected about a matter may not judge it and may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a general rule. A person who is not trusted about a certain halacha cannot serve as a judge or a witness about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule extends the idea of suspicion beyond buying and selling to court matters. If we do not trust a person to keep a halacha himself, we cannot rely on his ruling or his testimony about it.
steps.whatToRemember: Suspicion is limited to its own area, but within that area the suspected person cannot judge or testify.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
one who is suspect regarding a matter
may neither judge it nor testify about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל דָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person suspected about a matter may not judge or testify regarding that matter.

steps.title: Why is someone suspected about שביעית still trusted about מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's first ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why someone suspected about שביעית is not also suspected about מעשרות. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person ignores the laws of שביעית, we might expect him to ignore מעשר too. The גמרא wants to know what makes מעשר different.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why suspicion about שביעית does not carry over to מעשרות.

steps.title: מעשר must be eaten inside ירושלים, so it feels more serious
steps.stepSummary: שביעית produce may be eaten anywhere, but מעשר שני must be eaten inside the walls of ירושלים. That makes מעשר feel more serious to people.
steps.simpleTranslation: שביעית produce does not need to be eaten inside the wall of ירושלים. מעשר does need to be eaten inside the wall, so it feels more serious to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. Because מעשר has the strict requirement of being eaten in ירושלים, even a person who is lax about שביעית takes מעשר seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is about how serious each מצוה feels to the person. Eating only inside ירושלים is a visible, demanding requirement, so מעשר feels weightier than שביעית. This explains the first half of the משנה, that a person suspected about שביעית is still trusted about מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, which must be eaten in ירושלים
It is serious (strict) in his eyes

phrases.english: The Sabbatical Year produce does not require the wall,
phrases.notes: The wall of ירושלים. שביעית produce can be eaten anywhere.

phrases.english: tithe, since it requires the wall,
phrases.notes: This means מעשר שני, which may be eaten only inside ירושלים.

phrases.english: is stringent in his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעשר must be eaten within the walls of ירושלים, which makes it feel more serious than שביעית. So someone lax about שביעית is not assumed to be lax about מעשר.

steps.title: Why is someone suspected about tithes still trusted about the Sabbatical Year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a person suspected regarding מעשר, and asks for the reason behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one suspected about מעשר is not suspected about שביעית. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה's first ruling and asks why it is true. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 explained why a person suspected about שביעית can still be trusted with מעשר. Now the גמרא needs the reverse: why would someone who is careless with מעשר still be careful with שביעית?

keyTerms.meaning: A person suspected of not keeping a certain law
Tithe, a portion of produce that must be set aside
The Sabbatical Year and the special laws of its produce

phrases.english: One who is suspected regarding tithe.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says such a person is still not suspected about שביעית.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 6. Step 6 asked about the first half of the ruling; this asks about the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why suspicion about מעשר does not carry over to שביעית

steps.title: Tithes can be redeemed, but Sabbatical produce cannot
steps.stepSummary: מעשר can be redeemed, so people treat it lightly. שביעית produce stays forbidden with no way out, so it feels more serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר has a way of redemption. With שביעית, since it is forbidden to him and has no redemption, it feels strict to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by comparing how each law feels to an ordinary person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מעשר can be redeemed, a person might see it as something with a loophole and get careless. שביעית has no such escape route, so even a careless person may respect it. That is why suspicion does not travel from מעשר to שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption, swapping holy produce onto money so the produce itself becomes ordinary
It feels serious or strict to him

phrases.english: Tithe has redemption,
phrases.notes: He means the tithe produce can be swapped onto coins, so people may treat it as less serious.

phrases.english: the Sabbatical Year: since it is forbidden to him
and it has no redemption,
it is stringent in his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because מעשר has redemption and שביעית does not, שביעית feels more serious, so a person careless with מעשר may still keep שביעית.
steps.whatToRemember: Each direction has its own reason. שביעית feels lighter because it can be eaten anywhere (step 7). מעשר feels lighter because it can be redeemed (this step). So suspicion about one does not carry over to the other.

steps.title: Careless with Torah law means surely careless with rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: Someone suspected about שביעית or מעשר, which are Torah laws, is surely suspected about טהרות of ordinary food, which is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one suspected about either of these is suspected about טהרות. Since he is suspected about a Torah law, he is surely suspected about a rabbinic one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and explains it with a simple 'all the more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping ordinary food pure is a rabbinic rule, while שביעית and מעשר are Torah laws. If a person does not respect the stricter Torah laws, he will certainly not respect the lighter rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: A law from the Torah itself
A law made by the Sages

phrases.english: One who is suspected regarding this or regarding that.
phrases.notes: 'This or that' means שביעית or מעשר. The משנה goes on to say he is suspected about טהרות.

phrases.english: Since he is suspected regarding Torah law,
all the more so regarding rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲשִׁיד אַדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspicion about a Torah law carries over to a rabbinic law.

steps.title: Why is someone suspected about purity still trusted about the other laws?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's last clause, that some people are suspected about טהרות but not about שביעית or מעשר, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says there are people suspected about טהרות who are not suspected about the others. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's final clause and asks for its reason. This sets up a short answer and then a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of step 10. Step 10 showed that suspicion moves from Torah law down to rabbinic law. Now the גמרא asks why it does not also move up from rabbinic law to Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of keeping food ritually pure

phrases.english: And there are those suspected regarding ritual purity.
phrases.notes: The משנה finishes: they are not suspected about שביעית or מעשר.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the reverse direction of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why suspicion about טהרות does not carry over to שביעית and מעשר

steps.title: Careless with rabbinic law does not mean careless with Torah law
steps.stepSummary: Being careless with a rabbinic law does not prove a person is careless with Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, he is suspected about rabbinic law. About Torah law he is not suspected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: the 'all the more so' logic only works in one direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may take rabbinic rules lightly and still take Torah laws seriously. So suspicion about טהרות, which is rabbinic, does not spread to שביעית and מעשר, which are Torah laws.

phrases.english: Granted, he is suspected regarding rabbinic law,
regarding Torah law he is not suspected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suspicion about rabbinic law does not prove suspicion about Torah law.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to link purity and the Sabbatical Year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one trusted about טהרות is trusted about שביעית. That implies one suspected about טהרות is suspected about שביעית, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: one trusted about טהרות is trusted about שביעית. So if he is suspected about טהרות, he is suspected about שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties trust in טהרות to trust in שביעית. If they go together, then suspicion in טהרות should also mean suspicion in שביעית. That clashes with the משנה and with the answer in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'suspected' outright. The challenge comes from reading the opposite into it: if trusted means trusted, then suspected means suspected.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One who is trusted regarding ritual purity
is trusted regarding the Sabbatical Year,
so if he is suspected, he is suspected!
phrases.notes: Read it as: if he is suspected about טהרות, he is also suspected about שביעית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's last clause and the explanation given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one suspected about טהרות is not suspected about שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the opposite into the ברייתא: if trust in טהרות means trust in שביעית, then suspicion in טהרות means suspicion in שביעית.

steps.title: The משנה means a person seen being careful at home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעי says the משנה is talking about a person seen privately keeping שביעית and מעשר at home. So he stays trusted about them even though he is suspected about טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעי said: our משנה is talking about a case where they saw him behaving carefully in private, inside his home.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעי settles the contradiction by narrowing the משנה to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the normal rule: suspected about טהרות means suspected about שביעית. The משנה is an exception. This person was actually seen keeping these Torah laws in private, so we have direct evidence he is careful about them.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who answers the contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: Normally, suspicion about טהרות carries over to שביעית. The משנה's ruling applies only when the person was seen keeping these laws carefully at home.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that personal evidence about how someone actually behaves can outweigh the general rule about who is suspected.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai said:
Our משנה is when they saw him
practicing privately within his home.
phrases.notes: He means they saw him being careful with שביעית and מעשר at home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה applies to anyone suspected about טהרות, which would clash with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה applies only to one seen keeping these laws in private. The ברייתא gives the general rule.

steps.title: A broken promise makes him suspect about both
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל explains the ברייתא as a case where the person promised the חכמים to keep both laws and then broke one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל said: The case is a person who was suspected about both, came before the חכמים and promised to keep both, and later was suspected about one of them. Then we say: since he is suspected about this one, he is also suspected about the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the contradiction from Step 13, this time by explaining the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, being careless with טהרות would not make a person suspect about שביעית. In this case, though, he made a promise before the חכמים covering both laws and broke it. That shows his promise cannot be relied on, so he loses trust about both.

keyTerms.meaning: Took upon himself, promised to keep
Since, because of (this, then also that)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai son of Rabbi Yishmael said:
For example, where he was suspected about both,
phrases.notes: Both means טהרות and שביעית, the two laws from the ברייתא in Step 13.

phrases.english: and he came before the Sages
and promised to keep both of them,
and afterward he was suspected about one of them,
where we say: since he is suspected about this one,
he is also suspected about the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דַּהֲוָה חֲשִׁיד לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of Step 13. רבי אילעי explained the משנה, and this answer explains the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that anyone suspected about טהרות is suspected about שביעית, against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only speaks of someone who broke a promise before the חכמים covering both laws, so he is trusted about neither.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's ruling, that someone suspected about שביעית is not suspected about מעשר, is רבי עקיבא's view. The חכמים say he is suspected about מעשר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the view of רבי עקיבא, the unnamed author. But the חכמים say: one suspected about שביעית is suspected about מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's first ruling, about שביעית and מעשר, and tells us whose opinion it is and who disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a person careless about שביעית is still trusted about מעשר. רבי יוחנן says this is only רבי עקיבא's view. According to the חכמים, being careless about שביעית is enough to make him suspect about מעשר as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The unnamed one, the author behind unsigned teachings
The seventh year, when the land rests

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This is the view of Rabbi Akiva, the unnamed author,
phrases.notes: This means the משנה's line that one suspected about שביעית is not suspected about מעשר. Unsigned teachings usually follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית — חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: One suspected about the seventh year is suspected about tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְתִימְתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whose opinion the משנה's שביעית and מעשר line follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling follows רבי עקיבא. The חכמים hold that one suspected about שביעית is suspected about מעשר.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is meant by the חכמים who disagree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: which Sage holds the opposing view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: "חכמים" is a general title. The גמרא wants to know which specific תנא holds that being careless about שביעית makes a person suspect about מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, often meaning the majority view

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים mentioned in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is behind the view of the חכמים.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, whose area was strict about שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are רבי יהודה. In his area people treated שביעית as very serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, because in רבי יהודה's area they treated שביעית as strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים are רבי יהודה and explains why he holds this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's area, eating שביעית produce was seen as a major sin. So a person there who ignored שביעית had already crossed a serious line and could not be trusted about מעשר either.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, in his area

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda,
because in Rabbi Yehuda's area
the seventh year was treated as strict by them,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דִּבְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שְׁבִיעִית חֲמִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי יהודה. In his area שביעית was treated so strictly that someone who ignored it is not trusted about מעשר.

steps.title: A story shows how serious שביעית was there
steps.stepSummary: When one person insulted another as a convert, son of a convert, the other answered that at least he does not eat שביעית produce like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who called his friend "convert, son of a convert." The friend answered: I deserve a blessing, because I don't eat שביעית produce like you do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short story to prove that people in רבי יהודה's area saw eating שביעית produce as shameful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The insulted man fires back with the worst thing he can say: "you eat שביעית produce." That only works as a comeback if everyone there saw it as a serious sin. This supports the claim in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert, literally a resident or newcomer
May (a blessing) come to me, I deserve credit

phrases.english: as there was a certain man who would call his friend
"convert, son of a female convert,"
He said to him: I deserve a blessing,
since I do not eat seventh-year produce like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 18's claim that שביעית was treated strictly in רבי יהודה's area.
steps.raayaObject: That in רבי יהודה's area שביעית was considered very serious.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about people insulting each other, where eating שביעית produce is used as the sharpest comeback.

steps.title: Another version: the חכמים say the reverse
steps.stepSummary: A different report of רבי יוחנן's teaching: the חכמים say one suspected about מעשר is suspected about שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the view of רבי עקיבא, the unnamed author. But the חכמים say: one suspected about מעשר is suspected about שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי יוחנן's statement, where the חכמים's opinion is turned around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, being careless about שביעית made someone suspect about מעשר. Here it is the other way: being careless about מעשר makes someone suspect about שביעית. Both versions agree that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order. In Step 16, suspected about שביעית led to suspected about מעשר. Here, suspected about מעשר leads to suspected about שביעית.

phrases.english: There are those who say,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This is the view of Rabbi Akiva, the unnamed author,
but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: One suspected about tithes is suspected about the seventh year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of Step 16, with the חכמים's ruling reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, the חכמים hold that one suspected about מעשר is suspected about שביעית.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים in this version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks which תנא is meant by the חכמים, now in the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, this time about the second version, to set up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים's view is different in this version, it must belong to a different תנא. The גמרא now asks who that is.

phrases.english: And who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the חכמים's view in the second version.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר: suspected about one, suspected about all
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים in this version are רבי מאיר, who holds that one suspected about any one law is suspected about the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, who says: one suspected about one thing is suspected about the entire Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים here are רבי מאיר and gives his general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that being careless about any single law makes a person untrustworthy about every law. So naturally someone suspected about מעשר is also suspected about שביעית.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions say the משנה, which keeps suspicion about שביעית and suspicion about מעשר separate, follows רבי עקיבא. In the first version the חכמים say suspected about שביעית means suspected about מעשר, and they are רבי יהודה (his area was strict about שביעית). In the second version the חכמים say suspected about מעשר means suspected about שביעית, and they are רבי מאיר (suspected about one law means suspected about all).

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir, who says:
One suspected about one matter
is suspected about the entire Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: חָשׁוּד לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי חָשׁוּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי מאיר, who holds that one suspected about any law is suspected about the whole Torah.

steps.title: Two students argue over which version is correct
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה, students of רבי זעירא, disagreed about the two versions. Some say the pair was רבי יונה and רבי זעירא, students of רבי יוחנן. The first one begins: the חכמים say one who is חשוד on שביעית...
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה, the students of רבי זעירא (some say it was רבי יונה and רבי זעירא, the students of רבי יוחנן), argued about this. One of them said: "But the חכמים say one who is suspected about שביעית..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that two אמוראים argued over which of the two versions of רבי יוחנן's teaching is the right one. It begins quoting the first opinion, and that sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא gave two reports of רבי יוחנן's teaching without choosing between them. Now it shows that this was a real argument between named students. There are even two traditions about who those students were. The first speaker opens with the case of one who is חשוד on שביעית, which matches the wording of the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another tradition of the same report)
Suspected of not keeping a law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse רבי זעירא the teacher in the first tradition with רבי זעירא the student in the second. In the second tradition he is one of the two who argue, and their teacher is רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Yirmeya
students of Rabbi Zeira,
and some say it was
Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Zeira
students of Rabbi Yochanan,
one said:
but the Rabbis say
one who is suspected about שביעית
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. It continues on the next amud, following the first version of רבי יוחנן's teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָה וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה תַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי זְעֵירָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹנָה וְרַבִּי זְעֵירָא תַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After laying out two versions of רבי יוחנן's teaching, the גמרא now shows that two named students argued over which version is correct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two students disagreed about the exact wording of רבי יוחנן's teaching. The first begins with the version that speaks of one who is חשוד on שביעית.
